conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.scope: Credential-specific process-local admission and ownership registry shared across password-command calls and Tokio runtimes in one host, not a global service or general process manager.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.cleanupObservationBasis: The proposed three seconds reuses the existing recovery grace and is not a measured OS reap guarantee.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.admission: Count setup, running, output collection, cancellation, completed-but-unjoined work, and FAILED_HELD through ownership discharge. Retain the same-source barrier through cleanup. A queued caller uses its existing budget, launches no native work before admission, and does not enter an internal payload queue. Capacity pressure is not bad credentials and does not reset clocks.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.ownership: The native owner retains process scope, stdout and stderr pipes, cancellation, result publication, cleanup receipt, and thread completion independently of Tokio. Cancellation and result publication are atomic.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.output: Use nonblocking owned readers with no detached readers, partial credential publication, or new truncation policy. Preserve environment, working directory, shell parsing, complete UTF-8 trim, and nonzero behavior. Sanitize diagnostics.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.failure: Cleanup observation timeout or failure enters FAILED_HELD and retains the exact invocation registry record: slot, source reservation, owned Windows process and job handles or Unix unreaped leader, pipes, and worker-thread obligation. The owning host retains the record, closes affected admission, and reports a sanitized failure naming the obligation. It is not a cleanup receipt and does not authorize automatic restart, discarded ownership, a hidden forever worker, or a replacement cleanup queue. Permanently holding every ordinary Unix completion is not an adequate implementation.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.platform: Windows requires a private noninheritable job, documented process and primary-thread handles, suspended create and assign-before-resume, no breakaway fallback, explicit setup-failure cleanup, and observed process, zero-active-job, reader, and thread completion. Unix requires pre-exec group setup, the sole unreaped leader through the last signal, exact child reap, and no cached-PGID signal after reap, subreaper, global wait, process scan, or escaped-process action.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.unixReceipt: Establish a dedicated group before exec, retain the exclusive waitable unreaped leader through every mutating group signal, send the final signal while the anchor is valid, irreversibly revoke further signal authority, reap the exact leader, and use the former PGID only as a read-only observation key. Receipt requires conclusive platform absence, exact leader reap, completed or closed owned I/O, and native completion and join. Presence, denial, ambiguity, possible reuse, or errors retain the cleanup obligation without signal authority.
conditionalTechnicalRecommendation.platformProof: Execute real Windows and every claimed supported Unix target, including Linux and macOS if both remain supported. Compile-only or skipped runtime coverage is insufficient.

postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.historicalDisposition: Superseded by unixReceiptRecommendation after the single bounded API-level follow-up; retained for chronology and not the current technical recommendation.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.scope: Ordinary non-escaped Unix helpers, separate from intentionally escaped, persistent, or broker-created work.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.requiredProductionSequence: For each claimed Unix target, name the stable owned object, member-completion observation excluding the identity anchor, last signal, nonconsuming observation where needed, exact leader reap, identity release, and error behavior.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.forbiddenApproaches: Do not use PID, name, or ancestry scans, unrelated waits, a subreaper, global manager, cgroup, or coverage waiver.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.proofBoundary: Production API feasibility is required before implementation. Real-helper tests later corroborate implementation correctness and do not replace the production completion definition.
postPolicyTechnicalVerdict.notImpossibilityProof: No supported complete sequence has yet been supplied or justified. This does not assert that no platform-specific solution exists.

unixReceiptRecommendation.verdict: design-recommendation-ready; technically feasible with supported-API conditions
unixReceiptRecommendation.supersedes: The earlier blanket Unix ordinary-helper receipt feasibility blocker, but not its chronology.
unixReceiptRecommendation.groupLifetime: An ordinary non-escaped member keeps the original process group extant after leader reap, and reparenting does not erase its group membership. Conclusive later absence proves the original group ended. Later numeric reuse may produce conservative presence or error holds but cannot restore that group or confer signaling authority.
ordering: Establish a dedicated group before exec with leader PID equal to PGID and greater than one.
Retain exclusive waitable unreaped leader ownership through every mutating group signal; nonconsuming leader observation may be used.
Send the last termination signal while the identity anchor is valid, then irreversibly enter a no-more-group-signals state.
Observe and reap only the exact owned leader; ECHILD or competing reaping is an ownership error, not receipt.
After reap, use the former PGID only as a read-only observation key within the existing cleanup budget and never send it another nonzero signal.
Require exact leader reap, conclusive group absence, completed or closed owned I/O, and native completion and join before receipt and admission release.

linux.query: getpriority(PRIO_PGRP, P), never setpriority; clear thread-local errno before each call.
linux.absence: Only return -1 with errno ESRCH is conclusive absence.
linux.presence: Any successful result is presence, including nice value -1 with errno zero.
linux.inconclusive: EINTR permits read-only retry within the same budget. EPERM, EACCES, EINVAL, ENOSYS, unexpected errors, unknown context, or known ESRCH-fabricating sandbox or interposer behavior are not absence.
linux.limit: Require the native PID namespace and supported syscall semantics. Do not claim universal result-fabrication detection or use Linux kill(-P, 0) as the absence predicate.

macos.query: Supported libc POSIX/UNIX03 kill(-P, 0), not a private raw syscall or legacy non-POSIX variant.
macos.absence: Return -1 with ESRCH is conclusive absence under the supported POSIX-mode semantics.
macos.presenceOrInconclusive: Return zero is presence. EPERM, including unsignalable, MAC-denied, or zombie-only cases, is not absence.
macos.bindingProof: Implementation review and genuine runtime tests must verify the actual libc binding and supported-target conformance. Do not generalize the Linux getpriority predicate to macOS.

unixReceiptRecommendation.errorsAndRaces: Final SIGKILL failure, partial delivery, changed permissions, missed concurrent forks, surviving ordinary helpers, zombies, reparenting, or slow adopter reaping prevent receipt or retain a conservative hold. Telex reaps only its exact child and sends no post-reap catch-up signal.
unixReceiptRecommendation.failedHeld: After reap, FAILED_HELD retains the exact invocation record, slot, source reservation, responsible host, observation key, pipes, and native thread obligation, but no signal authority. It reports sanitized failure and permits no automatic restart, ownership discard, growing retry queue, or clean-exit claim.
unixReceiptRecommendation.proofBoundary: Campaign accepted this intended design. Product implementation and genuine Windows, Linux, and macOS runtime proof remain pending; existing tests are not proof of the new mechanism.

operatorShutdownDecision.question: For normal Telex host shutdown, may credential cleanup add up to 3 seconds after logical command/Wait completion, with admission closed and owned workers drained/joined; if receipt is still missing at that bound, should Telex report cleanup failure and retain ownership rather than report a clean exit?
operatorShutdownDecision.choiceSelected: Approve bounded orderly-exit drain and explicit failure hold (Recommended)
operatorShutdownDecision.approvedScope: Preserve logical command and Wait result deadlines. Normal exit of the host that owns credential work may take up to three additional seconds to close admission and drain and join owned workers concurrently against one absolute current cleanup budget.
operatorShutdownDecision.budgetLimits: Do not renew the budget per worker or multiply it by capacity. Waiting three seconds is not a cleanup receipt.
operatorShutdownDecision.missingReceipt: Report cleanup failure and retain named ownership and escalation, potentially beyond three seconds. Do not report clean exit or promise an unconditional three-second OS process-exit bound.
operatorShutdownDecision.ownershipLimit: Only the host owning credential work drains it. A client does not drain remote-host work, and Telex does not own preexisting external agents or broker-created work.
operatorShutdownDecision.notApproved: Measured performance, a universal finite OS cleanup guarantee, product implementation, runtime correctness proof, M2 completion, product writes, thread resolution, merge, and release remain unapproved.

items.source: PR #156 M2 Windows receipt implementation evidence from worker 38d183fb and its Windows platform delegate, with existing design steward documentary adjudication

evidence.evidenceLevel: Worker-supplied runtime evidence. The Local orchestrator verified all eight frozen artifact hashes, and the reconciler rechecked the packet index and checkpoint hashes. No one reran the tests or established source-to-binary exactness.
evidence.insidePollCleanup: After helper readiness and verified membership in the private invocation job, inside poll_cleanup immediately before it would return true, the retained leader handle was signaled and a successful accounting query reported ActiveProcesses 0, while the retained helper process handle with SYNCHRONIZE rights returned WAIT_TIMEOUT (258). In an isolated diagnostic the helper signaled about 1.4766 ms later without a second kill or fallback; that is not a maximum or acceptable delay. The assertion stops before return, so this does not show that the execution emitted a receipt or released admission.
evidence.afterRelease: Separate parent capacity and repeated-cancellation cases observed an unsignaled retained helper or shell handle after native-owner join, cleaned-scope drop including kill-on-close job closure, and registry removal. They did not record which process index failed or the later signal delay, and do not independently establish the membership or lag seen inside poll_cleanup.
evidence.results: Stronger module suite 7 passed, 3 failed, 1 child-only entry ignored; isolated diagnostic red; parent target 5 passed, 2 failed. Earlier green finite and grace cases polled both conditions and did not establish ordering.
evidence.provenanceLimit: Hashes freeze post-run artifacts only; no contemporaneous source-tree or executable digest was captured. Some raw API values, complete accounting buffers, per-operation timestamps, test PE architecture, and every member's final independent signaling are unrecorded.

stewardDocumentaryVerdict.conclusion: No documented guarantee was established that successful ActiveProcesses-zero accounting is ordered after every former member process object becomes signaled. No complete supported stronger production sequence is justified yet; this is not an impossibility proof.
stewardDocumentaryVerdict.codeSpecificAttribution: Pending the steward's review of the frozen packet for wrong job or handle, query failure or default zero, ABI or layout, handle reuse, and measurement-order errors.

evidence.scopeLimit: No harm, security impact, indefinite survival, repeated production leak, or general Windows lifetime conclusion is established.

consolidatedAdjudication.scope: The eight frozen files, prior canonical references, and read-only baseline checks only. No mutable worker reads, new research, experiment, or execution; the Local orchestrator and steward verified artifact hashes, not the originally executed source or binary.
consolidatedAdjudication.frozenCodeAssessment: The displayed code uses an explicit owned invocation job with checked assignment before resume, checks the accounting query result before reading it, uses a source-consistent x64 accounting layout, distinguishes wait results, and retains a SYNCHRONIZE-capable helper handle with verified job membership and no shown close or reopen. No wrong-job, failed or default-zero query, ABI or layout, wait-return, or handle-lifetime error was identified that explains away the report.
consolidatedAdjudication.evidenceSeparation: The A assertion runs before poll_cleanup returns true and is not itself a receipt or publication. B observes retained handles after join, cleaned-scope and job-handle drop, and record removal, and does not identify the failing role, job membership, or lag. Post-run snapshots cannot certify the originally compiled bytes.
consolidatedAdjudication.conclusion: Job accounting reaching zero is not a documented fence for completion of every member. No complete supported stronger production sequence is justified yet. This is not an impossibility, kernel-cause, continued-user-code, or harm claim, and it grants no new supervision machinery.
consolidatedAdjudication.remainingRequirement: A supported invocation-local completion barrier, or complete lifetime-safe member-handle ownership and observation covering all ordinary scoped descendants, including concurrent and short-lived ones, before receipt and admission release.

items.source: PR #156 M2 Unix platform delegate source analysis, with existing design steward interpretation

evidence.evidenceLevel: Source-only prediction. No macOS program was run, and all Linux and macOS runtime proof remains unrun. Only cross-target cargo check and clippy for x86_64-apple-darwin were reported.
evidence.details: In pinned XNU, process-group signaling skips zombies and POSIX behavior returns EPERM when no member is signalable. The frozen Unix implementation sends a mandatory final group SIGKILL while the leader is still unreaped, and returns any nonzero signal error, including EPERM, as cleanup failure. If ordinary successful completion leaves only the unreaped leader zombie, that signal could fail and hold an otherwise finished invocation, conflicting with the requirement that ordinary completions not remain permanently held.
evidence.stewardInterpretation: The steward reads the pinned zombie filtering and UNIX03 EPERM behavior as applying to the final SIGKILL, and recommends only that the anchored attempt result stay separate from the independent later receipt: record the attempt, seal signals, reap the exact leader, then require the full read-only absence, I/O, and join conjunction. The correction hold remains while campaign classifies authority.

consolidatedAdjudication.frozenCodeAssessment: The frozen Unix cleanup sends the final signal, seals further signals, and then propagates any nonzero SIGKILL error, including EPERM, as failure. That result is latched before the exact child reap and the post-reap observation, and the common owner then records the scope as failed and held, so the path cannot reach the independent receipt.
consolidatedAdjudication.conclusion: Because pinned XNU returns EPERM for a zombie-only group on a nonzero signal, this is a concrete conditional source defect in ordinary leaf completion. It is not an executed macOS failure or pass.
consolidatedAdjudication.proposedCorrection: For the justified macOS final-attempt EPERM case only: keep the error as attempt evidence, irreversibly seal signals, then proceed with bounded exact-owned leader reap and the independent post-reap absence, I/O, and join predicate. Post-reap EPERM stays Present, never absence. Ownership, setup, ECHILD, ABI, reap, and query failures are never ignored, and cancellation or command errors never become credential success.

items.description: Resolve the ordering between the anchored final group signal, the exact leader reap, and the later read-only absence check so ordinary macOS completions are not held by a zombie-only group.
items.affectedOutcome: The accepted Unix receipt sequence may hold ordinary successful macOS invocations if the final signal meets a zombie-only group.
items.requiredness: Required for the M2 repair in PR #156. Not an accepted limitation, waiver, or follow-up delivery.
items.sequencing: The Unix module and its original 22 tests stay unchanged. The steward's consolidated adjudication is complete; affected edits stay held until campaign classifies and approves the bounded correction, through reviewed Tier B reconciliation if it is material.
items.selectedDisposition: None selected; the steward's bounded attempt-record, seal, exact reap, and independent-absence correction awaits campaign classification and approval. Not authorized: treating EPERM as absence, signaling after reap, ignoring ownership errors, privilege or subreaper changes, a new agent, or a coverage waiver. The accepted post-reap read-only rule, where EPERM means presence or inconclusive, is unchanged.
